subject: MSA + Order Form: term notice ladder and termination-for-convenience workback (Aurelius)
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: sara.lowe@aurelius.com, contracts@aurelius.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: term notice ladder and termination-for-convenience workback (Aurelius)

Sara / Contracts team — thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our starting point (Aurelius_MSA_redline_v1.docx) with redlines focused on the term / renewal / termination sections. Key asks from your side we captured: 1) confirm auto-renew cadence, 2) align notice window for non-renewal, and 3) agree TfC mechanics for pilot/committed seats.

Quick summary of our proposal (high level):
- Term: 12-month initial term (Order Form).
- Auto-renew: 12-month renewals unless either party gives 90 days' notice prior to renewal date.
- Termination for convenience (TfC): mutual TfC permitted with 60 days' written notice; customer receives pro-rata refund for unused pre-paid subscription credits during wind-down.
- Offboarding support: 30 days standard support; extended support available as paid add-on.

Please review the attached redlines and call out anything you need changed. If Aurelius prefers a shorter notice window we can explore concessions (termination fees or extended support credits).

Next steps: 1) Sara, can you send your marked-up redline? 2) Laura (legal), happy to loop you for a quick read. 3) Marcus, please flag any commercial constraints.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aurelius_MSA_redline_v1.docx (redline)

From: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@aurelius.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@aurelius.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Apr 2025 11:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: term notice ladder and termination-for-convenience workback (Aurelius)

Karthik — thanks for sending the redline. We've reviewed internally and attached our edits (Aurelius_legal_redline_20250403.pdf). High-level feedback: 

- Auto-renew: Aurelius prefers a 12-month auto-renew but is asking for a 60-day notice window instead of 90. Their operational calendar makes 90 impractical for budget timing.
- Termination-for-convenience: Aurelius requests mutual TfC with 60 days' notice; they propose a 30-day wind-down obligation from Redwood and a refund of any prepaid unused months pro-rata.
- Pilot carveouts: for pilot seats we want a separate 30-day exit path with limited data-retention SLA.

We understand the commercial sensitivity and are open to a compromise. Please let us know if Redwood can accept 60 days for notice in exchange for a transition credit (one month of service) or a modest termination fee. 

Best,
Sara Lowe
Sr. Counsel, Aurelius Systems

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 04 Apr 2025 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: term notice ladder and termination-for-convenience workback (Aurelius)

Karthik / Marcus — quick legal read on Sara's asks. TL;DR: we should avoid moving from 90 -> 60 days without clear compensation terms. Notes: 

- Notice window: 90 days prior to renewal is our standard for committed 12-month contracts. It protects forecasting & capacity planning. Dropping to 60 days increases churn risk and makes replenishment harder.
- TfC: a mutual 60-day TfC is reasonable only if we retain a 60-day wind-down SLA (support + access) and offer only pro-rata refunds for prepaid, not credit for future discounts.
- Pilot carveouts: 30-day exit for pilots is acceptable, but require a data retention clause specifying 30 days of exported data availability and an additional 30 days of archival hold (no access) before deletion to satisfy compliance.

Recommended compromise options (internal):
1) Accept 60-day notice in exchange for one of: (a) termination fee equal to 1 month MRR, or (b) guaranteed 60-day paid transition support (at customer's TCV, not Redwood gratuitous).
2) Keep 90-day notice but offer an operational exception for pilots and named accounts with clearly defined carveouts in the order form.

I'll draft short memo with language variants (internal_memo_tfc_options.txt) you can use in the counteroffer. If Aurelius pushes, we should escalate to sales leadership for approval of a termination fee waiver.

- Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

> On Thu, Apr 3, 2025 at 11:08 AM Sara Lowe wrote:

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: term notice ladder and termination-for-convenience workback (Aurelius)

Team — commercial perspective: Aurelius is a mid-sized customer with strong potential ARR growth; being overly rigid risks losing them. I'm comfortable offering 60-day notice if we get either: (a) one-month termination fee (credited to onboarding costs), or (b) guaranteed 60-day paid transition support (billed at standard rates).

If legal signs off, I'll update pricing language in the order form. Please confirm which option we want to propose.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Manager, Strategic Accounts

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: term notice ladder and termination-for-convenience workback (Aurelius)

Sara — thanks for the quick turn. After internal discussion (cc: Laura + Marcus), Redwood can move forward with a compromise counteroffer. Proposed commercial/legal package (attached: Aurelius_counteroffer_v2.docx):

1) Auto-renew: 12-month renewals remain in place.
2) Notice window: reduce to 60 days prior to renewal (Aurelius request) for this Order Form only, subject to the following:
   - Customer agrees to a one-month transition credit (applied as a one-time invoice hold) OR pays a termination fee equal to one month MRR; Redwood will accept either as consideration for the shorter notice.
3) Termination-for-convenience: mutual TfC with 60 days' written notice. Redwood will provide 60 days of wind-down support (standard SLA); any additional extended support is billable. Pro-rata refunds for unused pre-paid months will be issued when applicable.
4) Pilot seats: maintain separate 30-day exit for pilot seats; data export window: 30 days active export + 30 day archival hold for compliance.

Next steps: Sara, can you confirm which consideration Aurelius prefers (transition credit vs termination fee)? If you accept in principle we'll prepare a tracked counter-redline and DocuSign package (link below). If you need the 90->60 change applied globally, we will need a senior-level approval and updated commercial terms.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/8942/deal/DEAL-8942
DocuSign (proposal): https://www.docusign.com/sign/xyz-aurelius-8942

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
